title: Tenant routing + TLS/KMS rotation upgrade checklist
content:
Purpose:

This doc is a working checklist and playbook for performing a coordinated upgrade that:
- switches tenant-aware routing from the legacy proxy adapter to the new in-runtime router
- rotates TLS certs and KMS keys used by private control plane components
- applies the updated Terraform module that changes networking resources (subnet tagging + firewall rules)

Context / motivation:
- Several customers run private deployments with a tenant-proxy in front of the runtime. The new in-runtime router (v2) reduces latency and simplifies prefix caching, but requires a staged rollout because it changes connection handshakes and header formats used by some legacy clients.
- We must also rotate TLS certs (short-lived cert rollout) and rotate KMS keys for signing tokens as part of compliance cycle PD-KMS-2025. Combining these activities reduces total downtime but increases blast radius; this playbook outlines safe sequencing and automated rollback gates.

High-level plan (phases):
1) Preflight (2-7 days before): verification and rehearsals
2) Silent deploy (canary 0.5% - 2% traffic) with shim translation enabled
3) Ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with staged KMS/TLS rotation windows per region
4) Post-migration validation and certificate deprecation
5) Rollback plan and postmortem

Preflight checklist (owner: Maya / SRE lead):
- [ ] Inventory customers using tenant-proxy (query telemetry + config store) — ensure list saved to PD-1973
- [ ] Run compatibility scan of client header expectations (script: tools/compat-check/scan-headers) against runtime v2 handshake (output attached)
- [ ] Validate Terraform module changes in a disposable lab (tf plan must be clean) — branch: feat/tenant-router-tf
- [ ] Create staging environment with mirrored KMS and short-lived certs (rotate interval 1h)
- [ ] Smoke tests: session establishment, token signing, prefix caching, streaming chunking under 1k token load
- [ ] Prepare rollback artifacts (old certs, old KMS key ARN, terraform rollback branch) and store in secure-ops vault path: secret/private-upgrades/tenant-router/rollback
- [ ] Schedule 3-hour maintenance windows with key customers and ensure CS notified

Terraform notes / safety knobs:
- Module to change: modules/networking/tenant-routing.tf (PR #409)
- Use tf workspace per-region to avoid accidental global changes
- Safety variable: enable_routing_v2 (default: false) — only flipped after runtime binary is present on nodes
- Use lifecycle "create_before_destroy" for firewall rule replacement where possible
- Example snippet for canary hosts tag (add to module vars):
  variable "canary_hosts" { type = list(string) default = [] }
  resource "google_compute_firewall" "tenant_canary_allow" {
    count = length(var.canary_hosts) > 0 ? 1 : 0
    name  = "tenant-canary-allow"
    source_tags = var.canary_hosts
    // ...
  }
- Plan to keep an immutable copy of previous state file for each region: state-backups/<region>/pre-tenant-router-YYYYMMDD.tfstate

KMS / TLS rotation sequencing (owner: Security eng - Rina):
- Rotate KMS keys in two phases: sign_key (used for tokens) then tls_key (used for certs). Reason: token signing rotation is faster to validate, cert rotation requires connection re-establishment.
- For each region:
  - Create new KMS key/version, grant read to control-plane service account, do NOT revoke old key yet
  - Deploy runtime binaries that support dual-signing (old_key || new_key) — feature flag: allow_dual_kms=true
  - Enable dual verification in control plane for 48h; monitor for token verification errors
  - Flip signing to new key (sign with new, verify with both)
  - After 72h with no errors, revoke old key and rotate to single-key verify (cleanup)
- TLS cert rotation: use short overlap window with dual cert acceptance in runtime (SNI + cert chains). Steps:
  - Upload new certs to secret manager, deploy CA bundle that includes both old and new roots
  - Start accepting new certs (accept_both_certs=true) while still serving old certs for existing sessions
  - Drain connections in waves per node (graceful drain 30s) to reduce half-open streams

Canary run details (owner: Ethan):
- Canary group selection: choose 2 low-impact tenants + internal QA tenants + 1 small external customer (consented)
- Enable runtime v2 behind feature flag but keep proxy shim in place (shim_mode = translate-headers)
- Traffic split config: route 0.5% initially. Increase only if no errors in X-Ray, logs, and quality checks.
- Metrics to watch (critical): 5xx rate, token verification errors, handshake latency p50/p95, token reissue rate, prefix-cache hitrate dip
- Health gate: if 5xx > 0.5% for 10m or token error spikes > 0.1% alert immediate rollback

Rollback choreography (owner: Diego):
- Trigger conditions: any fatal handshake/compat errors, unexpected KMS permission errors, TF plan showing destructive changes beyond firewall replace
- Fast rollback for runtime: roll nodes back using image rollback (image: runtime:v1.YYYYMMDD). Use canary -> region -> global rollback pattern.
- TF rollback: apply state-backed tf state file from state-backups/<region>/pre-tenant-router-YYYYMMDD.tfstate
- KMS/TLS rollback: re-enable old keys/certs and set allow_dual_kms=false after verification of stability
- Post-rollback: collect full logs, save into artifacts/rollback-<timestamp>.tgz, open PD-1973-ROLLBACK ticket and notify stakeholders

Tests and acceptance criteria (acceptance owner: QA lead):
- End-to-end token signing/verify tests pass for all client header shapes we know of
- Streaming session reconnection succeeds under spotty network (simulate 5% packet loss)
- No customer-facing errors for 48h after 100% ramp
- Telemetry showing steady or improved latency p95 and steady prefix cache hitrate

Open questions / todo:
- Confirm list of customers that require extended cert TTLs (TODO: CS outreach)
- Decide exact ramp durations per region (suggest 1h -> 6h -> 12h windows)
- Add terraform plan dry-run webhook to #private-deployments Slack for quick visibility

Post-migration cleanup:
- Remove shim translation code paths after 30 days of stable operations (risk: small subset of legacy clients may still send old headers)
- Rotate and retire temporary dual KMS key material
- Document change in internal upgrade catalog and update private-deployments runbook index

Appendix: quick rollback commands (examples)
- Runtime rollback (k8s): kubectl -n runtime set image ds/runtime runtime=redwood/runtime:v1.20250109 && kubectl rollout status ds/runtime -w
- Terraform rollback (example): terraform init && terraform workspace select us-west1 && terraform state pull > pre-rollback.tfstate && mv pre-rollback.tfstate terraform.tfstate && terraform apply -auto-approve
- Re-enable old KMS key (AWS CLI example): aws kms enable-key-rotation --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-1:123456789012:key/OLDKEYID

Notes to self: capture rehearsal logs, attach customer permission emails, and run the rehearsal twice in staging. This document is intentionally prescriptive but still a draft — input requested from security (Rina), SRE (Diego), QA (Ethan) before marking final.
